metadata.title: Pump System Units And Measurements
metadata.topic: SI measurement language for smart pump systems

learningPurpose: Prepare learners to read pump-system pressure, flow, temperature, power, and status measurements using explicit SI-unit expectations before moving into hydraulic calculations or monitoring data.

definitions.meaning: A named signal or reading used to represent one measured quantity in the pump-system learning context.
The unit expected internally by Industrial Learn calculation and simulation functions for the relevant quantity.

governingPrinciples: Pump-system measurement interpretation requires the quantity, value, unit, and measurement context to be stated.
Industrial Learn calculations and simulations must use consistent SI units internally.
A measurement label alone is not enough evidence for diagnosis.
assumptions: This knowledge file introduces measurement language only.
It does not interpret manufacturer pump curves or equipment ratings.
Any real pump-system reading requires supervised safety procedures and approved source evidence.
limitations: Does not teach pressure, flow, continuity, Bernoulli, pipe losses, pump selection, cavitation, or predictive diagnosis.
The DOE sourcebook is guidance rather than a current pump test standard.
No equipment-specific range, alarm threshold, or live-work procedure is authorised.

workedExample.title: Check a pump measurement row
workedExample.purpose: Show how to verify that a measurement row includes quantity, value, unit, and context before diagnosis.
given: Value is recorded as a number.
steps: Check that the unit matches the expected SI unit for the quantity.
Record whether the reading is ready for calculation or needs source-supported conversion.
workedExample.answer: The measurement is usable only when the quantity, value, unit, and context are explicit.

normalOperation: Measurement channels are interpreted only after their quantity, unit, and context are known.
commonMisconceptions: Treating a number without a unit as a usable measurement.
Treating kW and kWh as the same quantity.
Treating L/s and L/min as interchangeable without an explicit conversion.

faultConditions.title: Ambiguous measurement unit
symptoms: A pump-system reading is recorded without a unit or with a non-SI unit.
faultConditions.safeResponse: Do not use the reading for diagnosis until the unit and conversion evidence are confirmed.

safety.warning: A training measurement exercise does not authorise students to inspect, operate, adjust, or troubleshoot real pump equipment.
safety.studentBoundary: Students must use supervised laboratory or approved simulated data unless an authorised instructor provides real-system access.
